answer: of 76 faces reached only by a glob that names an ancestor, 76 are opened by some landing sweep, 76 are opened only by a sweeper no entry point runs again, and 0 are opened by no landing sweep at all. Across 9 landing modules and 13 glob calls, 9 calls open what they yield, 3 only read the name, 6 carry a pattern that is not a literal, and 2 modules only ever read the name (results/_r843bmc_inputs.py, scripts/e396_face_basename_suffix.py).
limits: one hop only: the treatment is the loop body's treatment of the loop variable, so a yield that is renamed (``rel = os.path.relpath(p)`` then ``open(rel)``) is graded on the first hop and reads as a name use, not as an open

a computed pattern (``f + '/**/*'``) is published as not-a-literal: the landing it performs was measured by E609, but the pattern text here cannot be matched back to a face path, so it contributes no treatment to any face
the population is machine-read from E609's and E613's published faces; a stale upstream face would be graded as published, and population_note says where it came from
literal openers elsewhere in the corpus are E606's measurement and are not re-derived here -- this face prices only what the landing sweeps do with what they glob
a module is 'live' when E611's classifier finds an entry point naming its basename; a reference composed from a string is a miss
population_note: read from the published E609/E613 faces
population_source: results/state_tilt/GLOBSWEEPREACH.json (E609 ancestor-only faces) + results/state_tilt/ANCESTORRERUNS.json (E613 landing modules)
